overrides.replacement_claim: Aggregate sprint projections used by the performance status API, server-rendered workbench, and TUI omit durable operational lifecycle and cancellation state because they bypass the enriched PerformanceStatus use case.
overrides.reason: Both theories identify the same projection defect. The aggregate helper delegates directly to the state projection, the sprint summary stores that result, and the web status route and presentation surfaces consume it without durable-run enrichment.

overrides.replacement_claim: The performance evidence endpoint has a compatibility path that returns an unversioned ad hoc artifact payload instead of PerformanceEvidenceResult.
overrides.reason: The fallback branch explicitly serializes attempt_id, artifacts, and returned_count without schema_version or the versioned evidence DTO fields, and the separate optional evidence interface makes this branch reachable.

overrides.replacement_claim: The public performance configuration table documents hard maxima above values that runtime validation permits.
overrides.reason: The documentation advertises several hard maxima above defaults, while validation uses the defaults themselves as ceilings and rejects larger values.

overrides.replacement_claim: PerformanceResult returns an unclassified raw error when no terminal result exists, bypassing performance-specific transport error mapping.
overrides.reason: The unavailable-result branch returns a plain error, while the performance HTTP mapping recognizes only PerformanceUseCaseError values.

overrides.replacement_claim: sharedOperationRunner discards errors from performanceSettings, allowing dispatch to proceed after invalid effective performance configuration.
overrides.reason: Both theories describe the same swallowed setup error. The runner discards the third return value even though performanceSettings can fail duration parsing or limit validation; the stronger duplicate evidence establishes the static failure path despite unsuccessful earlier reproducer attempts.

overrides.replacement_claim: The performance CLI maps every non-cancellation performance failure to ExitValidation regardless of its classified category.
overrides.reason: The command writer handles context cancellation separately and unconditionally wraps every other classified performance error with ExitValidation, losing category-appropriate CLI exit behavior.

overrides.replacement_claim: The performance failure path can publish flow-state after its verification writer token becomes stale because no fence check occurs immediately before SaveFlowState.
overrides.reason: Both theories describe the same writer-fencing gap. The failure path checks ownership during state publication, then loads and saves flow state without another check, while SaveFlowState is independently unfenced.

overrides.replacement_claim: ValidateRepairReverification accepts malformed nested performance TargetResults because it validates only top-level performance reverification fields.
overrides.reason: TargetResults are persisted, but the validator's performance branch returns without validating target identities, qualifications, comparisons, or nested outcomes.

overrides.replacement_claim: The JSON performance-output parser accepts malformed trailing content after a valid envelope.
overrides.reason: The parser rejects a second successfully decoded JSON value but accepts every second-decode error rather than requiring io.EOF, so malformed trailing syntax is accepted.

overrides.replacement_claim: Public performance evidence intentionally exposes bounded metadata references, including paths and digests, while withholding artifact contents and raw output.
overrides.reason: The supplied documentation explicitly promises bounded evidence references and metadata, and the public schema description permits references while prohibiting raw samples, output, profiles, patches, prompts, payloads, environment values, and secrets. No supplied criterion forbids metadata paths or digests themselves.

overrides.replacement_claim: The TUI exposes mutating performance actions for a disabled project when a historical performance attempt exists.
overrides.reason: The outer navigation condition admits either enabled policy or any existing attempt, then always adds start and adds resume, cancel, and recover when an attempt ID exists. Existing tests cover disabled policy only without an attempt.

overrides.replacement_claim: Disabled-policy validation falsely reports a performance policy mismatch for fenced or HTML-commented Performance Targets pseudo-headings that target parsing correctly ignores.
overrides.reason: Both theories identify the same inconsistent heading detection. ParsePerformanceTargets excludes fences and comments, but markdownHeadingPresent does not track those contexts and its result independently triggers the disabled-policy mismatch.

overrides.replacement_claim: Performance manifest discovery accepts descriptor markers separated from their function declaration by blank lines or comments despite requiring immediate precedence.
overrides.reason: The discovery loop retains a pending marker while skipping blank and comment lines, contradicting the explicit immediate-precedence contract.

overrides.replacement_claim: Performance-specific defaults and lower-only policy validation are implemented in the generic platform config package contrary to the platform domain-neutrality rule.
overrides.reason: The platform package defines performance workflow defaults and requirements-aware lower-only validation, while the architecture criterion explicitly reserves product defaults and validation rules for the owning product module.

issues.claim: Aggregate performance projections omit durable lifecycle and cancellation facts.
issues.title: Performance status surfaces omit durable run state
issues.reason: The API, workbench, and TUI consume an aggregate projection that bypasses durable-run enrichment, so active and cancellation-requested runs appear operationally incomplete.

issues.claim: Historical attempts cause disabled projects to expose mutating TUI actions.
issues.title: Disabled performance policy still exposes TUI mutations
issues.reason: An existing attempt ID bypasses policy gating and exposes start, resume, cancel, and recover operations.

issues.claim: The evidence endpoint can return an unversioned fallback response incompatible with its normal DTO.
issues.title: Evidence API fallback violates the versioned response schema
issues.reason: Adapters lacking the optional evidence capability receive a successful response with a different unversioned shape.

issues.claim: The performance CLI collapses distinct operational failures into ExitValidation.
issues.title: Performance CLI loses category-specific exit behavior
issues.reason: Runtime, timeout, persistence, dependency, and configuration failures become indistinguishable from validation failures at the process boundary.

issues.claim: Unavailable performance results bypass typed performance error translation.
issues.title: Missing performance result returns an unclassified error
issues.reason: The raw unavailable-result error falls through the performance-specific HTTP mapper and loses the intended stable code and category.

issues.claim: Product-specific performance policy is owned by the platform config package.
issues.title: Platform config contains bounded-context performance policy
issues.reason: Performance workflow defaults and lower-only validation reside in a package required to remain domain-neutral.

issues.claim: Persisted repair performance target results are not structurally validated.
issues.title: Repair reverification accepts malformed nested performance results
issues.reason: Malformed target identities, qualification data, comparisons, or outcomes can pass persisted-state validation when top-level authority fields are valid.

issues.claim: Descriptor discovery permits intervening blank or comment lines after a marker.
issues.title: Descriptor markers need not immediately precede functions
issues.reason: The scanner skips intervening lines while retaining the marker, accepting mappings outside the documented closed descriptor form.

issues.claim: A stale performance writer can publish the failure summary to flow state.
issues.title: Failure summary publication is not writer-fenced
issues.reason: Ownership may change after fenced state publication and before the independently unfenced SaveFlowState call, allowing a stale generation to overwrite current workflow state.

issues.claim: Documented hard maxima exceed the values accepted by configuration validation.
issues.title: Performance limit documentation contradicts validation
issues.reason: Operators following the documented maxima receive configuration-loading failures because validation caps values at defaults.

issues.claim: Malformed trailing bytes after a valid performance JSON envelope are accepted.
issues.title: Performance JSON parser does not require EOF
issues.reason: A non-EOF syntax error from the trailing decode is treated as acceptable, weakening the closed output schema.

issues.claim: Pseudo Performance Targets headings trigger disabled-policy mismatch findings.
issues.title: Policy validation misclassifies fenced and commented headings
issues.reason: Declaration detection does not apply the parser's fence and comment exclusions, producing false validation failures.

issues.claim: sharedOperationRunner ignores invalid performance settings instead of failing setup.
issues.title: Operation runner swallows performance configuration errors
issues.reason: Duration parsing and limit-validation errors disappear before dispatch, allowing operations to proceed with invalid or partial settings.
